newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon index breaks 2,000, led by Cerebos.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon index breaks 2,000, led by Cerebos.

text.p: Singapore stocks continued lower in sluggish trading with the key Straits Times Industrials (STI) index breaking the pschological 2,000 support at noon.
At 0430 GMT, the index was down 15.42 points at 1,999.36. Turnover was moderate, around 52 million shares with 80 gainers to 150 losers.
The fall was mainly due to index linked Cerebos Pacific plunging Singapore $1 to S$7 after it reported flat first half earnings and warned of a tougher second half.
"The results are far worse than expected, many houses are downgrading it," an analyst with a European brokerage said.

Another dealer said sentiment was gloomy with most investors sidelined. "There is just no good reason to buy Singapore. But it's not just Singapore. Most funds are staying away from Asia where sentiment has been depressed by Thailand."
Singamas Container Holdings Ltd shares are suspended pending an announcement. Shares of the container maker were active and hit a new year high of HK$1.11 on Tuesday.
Newly listed telephone cable manufacturer Huan Hsin ended the morning session at US$0.465 against its initial offer price of US$0.42 on volume of over 10 million units.
